# N11 current native source port

Source preparation only. The narrow retention correction has12 portable data/
real-file tests passing; no .NET, compiler, native procedure, CI action or Git
mutation was executed. Ordinary product qualification remains closed.

## Entry and prerequisites

The shared [bridge](bridge.py) uses case-sensitive JSON member names through
`pairs(items)` and `decode(raw)`. Exact duplicate names are rejected at every
depth, including different JSON escapes that decode to the same name. Distinct
Linux file/directory map names such as `Assets` and `assets` are preserved.
Closed receipt, image and packet schemas still reject extra or differently
cased outer fields; field types, byte bounds, hashes and modes are unchanged.
The [focused parser controls](../../test_json_keys.py) include actual source44
None build-map rows and exact-duplicate/closed-field negative neighbors for
both bridges. Passing data controls establishes no N11/N12 native outcome.

`adapter.execute(context, *, deadline)` uses the same13-key root context as the
[owner-death bridge](../owner-death/README.md#entry-contract). It adopts the shared
dispatcher's existing root-owned0700 output containing exactly the five root600
plan/source/build/inventory/execution inputs, checks bindings and creates all new
leaves exclusively. It returns one exact case row for **N11 only**.

The full current capture and actual CLI/helper locked-restore/Release-publication
logs/maps are verified with [binding.py](../../binding.py). The genuine peer helper
comes from the current receipt's helpers.peer.image and is retained through
[slot/helpers.py](../slot/helpers.py). Both historical N02 and N03 prerequisites
still execute physically; they receive no duplicate case credit.

The shared [bridge](../n11/bridge.py) stages full actual inputs via the frozen
owner-death copy helpers with source_sealed=False. Source stays0700 directories/
0644-or0755 files; tool/runtime/helpers are0555 directories/0444-or0555 files. The
runtime is an actual compact FDD deployment, never a fake inventory of an SDK.
The original family shell creates its own request/workspace.

The real [OS audit](../os_audit.py) is called on one capped absolute deadline:
Audit(end), initialize_tools(), then build(runtime,tool,False,peer). The original
[runner](../native_process.py), literal dispatch/FIFO EOF joins, native shell and
retention collector preserve original root-unit/process ownership and cleanup.
No old build schema, TRX, source-review Boolean or successful native result is
fabricated. The N02 actor derives from the actual current checkout UID/GID and
is checked against real NSS; the root adapter cannot substitute a protected owner.

## Native behavior and clocks

N11 is the real synchronous factory stall and preserved quarantine. Its historical
failed/false-settlement record remains one supported outcome. A separate strict
data outcome now describes **worker lifecycle fail-stop, then root physical
settlement** when the callback's original bounded stop path reaches the fixed
fail-fast and the root later records physical settlement. The root stop is not
claimed as the cause of worker exit. The canonical [N11 checkpoint goal](../../../../docs/plans/issue-779-csharp-supervision-migration.md#checkpoint-1-one-real-supervised-worker)
and source-owned [`StopAndJoinAsync`](../../../../Evidence/ForgeTrust.AppSurface.Evidence.Contracts/EvidenceWorkerExecution.cs#L505),
[`WaitWithinStopDeadlineAsync`](../../../../Evidence/ForgeTrust.AppSurface.Evidence.Contracts/EvidenceWorkerExecution.cs#L588),
and [`FatalTermination`](../../../../Evidence/ForgeTrust.AppSurface.Evidence.Contracts/EvidenceWorkerExecution.cs#L701)
describe the lifecycle. The fixed callback message is emitted only after the
original bounded callback join fails; the retained worker stderr must also carry
the three source method tokens.

`check_stall_record(record, *, worker_stdout, worker_stderr, expected_generation,
expected_pid, expected_starttime_ticks, expected_uid, expected_gid,
expected_descriptor_sha256, expected_stopping_ms=None)` retains its original
failed/false-settlement contract and result schema. Use
`check_callback_failed_settled_record` with the same arguments only for the
strict settled-callback record. It requires failed=false, physical settlement,
all original startup/stop/pending-start joins, `first_failure=None`, completed
monitor, terminal code3/status6, the exact armed/entered/no-disposer stream,
the fixed fail-fast message and stack tokens, joined EOF/byte/hash/pump checks,
empty final cgroup data, and both full timing proofs within the original stop
and job allowances. It returns a separate closed consistency schema with the
actual publication time and fixed lifecycle outcome label. Both checkers are
detached data validators and return native authority/acceptance false.

`stall_capture.parse_original` selects the new checker from the original frame's
physical-settlement bit and requires the exact bounded ASEVD410/worker-terminal
failure context. It never retries the legacy checker after a new-branch failure.
`records.py` reparses the retained original frame and requires the matching
closed consistency schema and exact byte bindings. Neither schema waives the
source, image, identity, pump, cgroup, NSS, quarantine, output, or deadline
checks. Portable controls establish data consistency only; a fresh complete
Linux capture remains required for native N11 credit.

Fixture600/cleanup30 remain unchanged. N11 creates the original240-second request once and selects its owner runtime from that original remaining budget.
The earlier outer absolute deadline remains in force; no native retry or renewed
allowance is introduced. A fixture failure stays failed even if retention succeeds.

## Evidence and reconciliation

`validate_evidence(context,evidence_raw,*,capture_raw)` checks only the bounded
current-source envelope. It establishes no physical fact. The mandatory
`verify_retained_evidence(context,*,deadline)` rereads actual retained leaves,
command metadata and logs and repeats all original readable record predicates
in [records.py](records.py). Run and aggregate must require both exact rows equal;
execute also performs retained reconciliation itself before returning.

N11-evidence.json binds the original USTAR digest and every unchanged
raw member. The actual collector writes control/native.tar; its stdout is only a
terminal marker. The adapter reads the actual bounded archive, validates it without
filesystem extraction, retains it byte-exact as native-private.tar, and retains each
fixed leaf individually. Aggregate rereads both the actual archive and those leaves;
neither the hash nor the record-validator input is reconstructed from member data.
Original8MiB member/32MiB payload bounds remain; the archive has its separate
33,619,968-byte header/padding bound. Raw records are not echoed; no coverage or
counter arithmetic is performed. The N12 adapter imports the fixed N11 bridge
read-only, bound by the complete current capture.

### Retention helpers and pitfalls

The [bridge](bridge.py) exposes internal data/file helpers used by both adapters:

- `save_archive(path,raw,*,deadline)` exclusively creates only native-private.tar
  in the caller-owned0700 output, uses the separate archive bound, and checks
  opened/named file and parent identity through fsync under the original deadline.
  Production prerequisites already require the caller and output to be root0:0.
- `validate_commands(commands)` requires exactly two terminal command records,
  each with exactly one ordinal-stdout.log and one ordinal-stderr.log row. Stream
  byte counts are integers in0..8MiB and SHA values are64 lowercase hex characters.
- `verify_commands(output,commands,*,deadline)` rereads both real command records
  and both streams, even when their recorded length is zero. Missing/duplicate
  stream rows, missing files, changed bytes, symlinks and hardlinks cannot skip a read.
- Private `validate_packet(...,*,archive_raw,deadline)` requires the actual original
  archive bytes, their exact packet digest and matching member projection before
  forwarding those same bytes to the unchanged record predicates.

Use the actual retained callback for reconciliation; the detached envelope checker
alone cannot establish a physical fact. A Python USTAR reserialization can have the
same members and different bytes, so it must never stand in for original custody.
The [portable controls](../../test_n11.py) exercise metadata and ordinary files only;
their success does not qualify a Linux native case or simulate a protected owner.

## Source audit and remaining work

[port-manifest.json](port-manifest.json) records relative historical paths, hashes,
source files and static invariance. [historical-to-current.patch](historical-to-current.patch)
shows only the historical provenance boundary replacement and sixth env literal.
The historical patch records the initial port only. The settled-callback
correction updates two entries in the native shell's fixed parser-hash array to
match the reviewed modules and [parser-pins.tsv](parser-pins.tsv). The dispatcher
and retainer remain unchanged. The
`check_stall_record` historical data contract remains supported; the current
parser and capture modules now add the separate strict settled-callback contract
described above. `validate_n11_capture` recomputes that contract from the original
bytes; the other identity, custody and quarantine predicates remain in force.
The [parser-pin controls](../../test_n11_parser_pins.py) bind all four literal
names and hashes to the TSV and current file bytes, then exercise the original
row/count guards with modeled custody calls. Wrong hash/order, missing/extra
rows and extra columns reject. This is a data consistency check; physical root
custody still requires the genuine Linux procedure.
Parent/Godel owns inventory registration. Independent review, portable validation,
actual current helper publication and fresh Linux native execution remain required.
No all16-ready or coverage-gain claim is made.

## Failed-fixture archive retention

When a fixture fails but its existing bounded retainer supplies the actual
archive, `execute_case` saves the unchanged bytes as `native-private.tar` before
rethrowing the original fixture exception. The failure-only save shares the
archive read's `retain_end`; it adds no clock or allowance. Expiry, an occupied
destination or an I/O save failure cannot replace the original fixture failure.
This path creates no successful evidence packet or case result, and the existing
success-path save and validation remain unchanged. The
[portable failure-retention controls](../../test_failed_fixture_retention.py)
exercise the actual orchestration block with ordinary owned files and detached
command outcomes; they establish no native or protected-owner fact.
